hardGateFindings.finding: The controls consistently preserve hiring-reader, collaborator, audience, application, and hiring outcomes as not-yet-measured. Reader research, solicitation, and job-search follow-through remain planned with no returned receipts.

All eight blind spots have distinct signals, control artifacts, triggers, owners, decision rules, next tests, and evidence-return paths. Live graph counts, exact-set role classifications, render-derived composition inventories, dated mosaic review, and receipt state machines make the controls testable.

The judge protocol and deterministic checker require separate bundle-bound artifacts and orchestration receipts with distinct session identifiers, read-only independent-agent mode, generatorWasJudge false, timestamps, and artifact hashes. The repository expressly describes this provenance as auditable process evidence rather than cryptographic proof.

Record-level schemas and redacted citation generation exclude protected locators and private source content, while the current whole-graph mosaic review identifies aggregation risks and mandates minimization. External receipt validation rejects identifying feedback fields, and no private feedback or relationship graph is published.

limitations: This is an LLM repository-control evaluation, not human reader research, collaborator review, deployment approval, application evidence, or a hiring outcome.
External outcomes remain not-yet-measured; the planned reader study, hiring-reader solicitation, and job-search follow-through have no returned receipts in this bundle.
Repository provenance and distinct-session receipts are auditable process evidence, not cryptographic proof of evaluator independence or authorship.
The mosaic receipt is an internal control review, not legal, participant, collaborator, or human privacy approval.
